quotes.text: The only way to get rid of a temptation is to yield to it.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.comment: Darling, your boredom is just cowardice dressed in Prada. Do something interesting.

quotes.text: I don't know what's the matter with me. I'm restless.
quotes.author: Virginia Woolf
quotes.comment: Virginia felt restless too. She wrote 9 novels. What's your excuse?

quotes.text: The heart was made to be broken.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.comment: Oscar knew. He loved unwisely. At least you're not in Reading Gaol, so cheer up.

quotes.text: I cannot fix on the hour, or the spot, or the look, or the words, which laid the foundation. It is too long ago. I was in the middle before I knew that I had begun.
quotes.author: Jane Austen
quotes.comment: Elizabeth Bennet fell slowly. You fell stupidly. There's a difference.

quotes.text: Better never to have met you in my dream than to wake and reach for hands that are not there.
quotes.author: W.B. Yeats
quotes.comment: Yeats pined for Maud Gonne for 30 years. She never loved him back. Still, he won a Nobel Prize. Perspective, love.

quotes.text: Annual income twenty pounds, annual expenditure nineteen nineteen and six, result happiness. Annual income twenty pounds, annual expenditure twenty pounds ought and six, result misery.
quotes.author: Charles Dickens
quotes.comment: Stop buying £5 coffees, darling. You are not Dickens. You're just broke.

quotes.text: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.
quotes.author: Jane Austen
quotes.comment: Jane understood. Marry rich. Problem solved. (Kidding. Kind of.)

quotes.text: There is no such thing as a moral or an immoral book. Books are well written, or badly written. That is all.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.comment: Oscar never got bored because he read good books. Unlike you, scrolling Instagram.

quotes.text: I am so clever that sometimes I don't understand a single word of what I am saying.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.work: The Happy Prince and Other Tales
quotes.comment: At least Oscar's confusion was witty. Yours is just tragic.

quotes.text: I am not young enough to know everything.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.comment: Wilde knew he didn't know it all. You think you do. That's the tragedy.

quotes.text: Vanity working on a weak head, produces every sort of mischief.
quotes.author: Jane Austen
quotes.comment: Jane wrote this about Emma Woodhouse. She'd have a field day with your LinkedIn bio.

quotes.text: I have nothing to declare except my genius.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.comment: Oscar said this ironically at customs. You say it unironically on Twitter. See the problem?

quotes.author: George Orwell
quotes.comment: You want power? Orwell showed where that leads. Spoiler: dystopia.

quotes.text: All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others.
quotes.author: George Orwell
quotes.comment: Climbing the ladder? Remember: the pigs became the farmers. Mind the sty.

quotes.text: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.comment: Oscar was literally in prison when he understood this. Your 'gutter' is a Monday. Perspective.

quotes.text: The cure for anything is salt water: sweat, tears, or the sea.
quotes.author: Isak Dinesen (but often attributed in British circles)
quotes.comment: Cry, work out, or book a flight to Cornwall. Pick one and stop wallowing.
